instruction: Increase the width of the title 'Product Comparison' on page 2 to span the full width of the slide.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing title width to span full slide on slide 2. Verified original: width=8229240, slide_width=9144000. Expected: width >= 8800000 EMUs (approximately 96% of slide width).

llm_judge_reasons: Fragile text matching: Getter searches for shapes containing 'Product Comparison' text. If user modifies the title text while resizing (e.g., adds punctuation, changes case, or edits text), the getter will fail to find the shape and return None, causing incorrect verification failure.
The instruction only requires increasing width, not preserving exact text, so text changes should be tolerated.
The min_width threshold of 8800000 EMUs (~96% of slide width) is somewhat arbitrary for 'full width' - could reasonably expect closer to 100%.
Core verification logic is sound: correctly targets slide index 1 (page 2), extracts width property, compares numerically, and has appropriate postconfig to save file.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use position-based or placeholder-type matching instead of text content matching. For example, check for title placeholder on the slide using shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE.
Alternatively, use shape position heuristics: the title is typically the topmost or largest text shape on the slide.
Consider increasing min_width threshold to ~9000000 EMUs (~98-99% of slide width) for more accurate 'full width' verification.
Add fallback logic: if no shape contains 'Product Comparison', check all text shapes on the slide and return the one with maximum width (assumes user resized the title even if text changed).
